title: A Balcony Garden During Water Restrictions
script: Anwar: [warmly] Leila, the city has announced water restrictions. Should we stop our balcony garden?
Leila: Not necessarily, but we need to reduce waste and follow the allowed watering times.
Anwar: [concerned] Several pots become dry by midday because the balcony faces west.
Leila: We can move sensitive plants behind the shade screen and group pots so they lose moisture more slowly.
Anwar: [honestly] Should we water a little every few hours?
Leila: That can waste water. Check the soil below the surface, then water deeply only when the plant needs it.
Anwar: [relieved] I have been watering the leaves because they look hot.
Leila: Aim near the soil. Wet leaves in strong sun do not solve dry roots.
Anwar: [thoughtful] Can we reuse any household water?
Leila: Clean water from rinsing vegetables can be collected, if it contains no soap, oil, or unsafe material.
Anwar: [reflective] What about water from washing dishes?
Leila: Not for these food plants unless local guidance says it is treated safely. We should not guess.
Anwar: [peacefully] We could also add a layer of dry leaves on top of the soil.
Leila: Yes, mulch can reduce evaporation, but keep it away from the main stem and watch for pests.
Anwar: [encouraging] Which plants should we protect first?
Leila: The herbs we use, the young tomato, and the native flowering plant. We may pause new planting.
Anwar: I feel sad about removing two decorative plants.
Leila: [warmly] We can offer them to a neighbor with a shaded ground garden instead of letting them die here.
Anwar: That is better. I will make a watering chart based on the restriction schedule.
Leila: And I will label the safe collected water. Conservation works best when everyone knows the system.
Anwar: [gently] Our balcony may look smaller this season, but it can still be healthy.
Leila: Exactly. Caring for plants also means responding honestly to the limits of our environment.

quiz.question: Why must the garden plan change?
quiz.explanation: Limited water requires a more careful routine.

quiz.question: How can they reduce moisture loss?
options: Place every pot in full sun

quiz.question: What reused water may be suitable?
quiz.explanation: Only clearly safe household water is considered.

quiz.question: What will they do with some decorative plants?
options: Offer them to a neighbor with more shade
quiz.explanation: Relocation may preserve plants with less water.

quiz.question: What is the key environmental lesson?
options: Care must respect real resource limits
Gardens matter more than water rules
Every season needs the same plan
quiz.explanation: Responsible gardening adapts to local conditions.

quiz.question: Why is frequent light watering questioned?
options: It may waste restricted water without reaching roots effectively
quiz.explanation: The plan targets need rather than habit.

quiz.question: What condition makes rinse water potentially reusable?
options: It contains no soap, oil, or unsafe material
It has been stored for a week

quiz.question: Why is local guidance important for dishwater?
options: Food plants should not receive guessed or unsafe reused water
quiz.explanation: Reuse must follow actual treatment and health rules.

quiz.question: How does mulch help and create a new duty?
options: It reduces evaporation but requires spacing and pest checks
quiz.explanation: A useful method still needs correct use and observation.

quiz.question: Why offer decorative plants to a neighbor?
options: A shadier site may keep them alive without spending scarce water
quiz.explanation: Relocation matches plants with a more suitable environment.
